correctness.rationale: Let S be the 91 length-45 factors of tau^9(0), itself length 274. The finite certificate directly verifies every length-45 factor of tau(s) for s in S belongs to S. Because the substitution is nonerasing, any length-45 output factor of a sufficiently long input occurs within tau of some length-45 input factor, so closure inductively proves S is the complete length-45 factor language of the infinite fixed point. Each triple condition is a Boolean predicate on one such factor. Exhaustively evaluating all 13244 triples over S is therefore a valid infinite-position proof, not a test of 274 observed positions. Fresh independent reconstruction found 91 factors, closure PASS and exactly 55 valid triples; distinguished lexicographic order from ascending maximal-shift order. Original census.json was checked against generated certificate by source verifier; arbitrary shifts beyond 44 are not tested.
residual_risks: No claim beyond c=44: the full Open Problem 30 of classifying all pseudoperiods remains open.
The closure argument requires all 91 factors, non-erasing morphism and the 45-window length, not a bounded prefix alone.

value.rationale: This finite initial classification addresses a published difficult automatic-word open problem at a natural substitution length scale, and unlike raw prefix testing it rigorously certifies every infinite position. The complete 55-table and positive/negative witnesses provide a reusable computational and structural benchmark for a future full algorithm.
residual_risks: Its value is deliberately bounded by the c<=44 initial window; further unbounded structure is not established.

final_claim: For infinite Tribonacci substitution word tau(0)=01, tau(1)=02, tau(2)=0, the exact set of triple shifts 1<=a<b<c<=44 satisfying t_i in {t_(i+a),t_(i+b),t_(i+c)} at every i>=0 comprises 55 triples out of C(44,3)=13244. The next maximum shift after (4,6,7) is 11, realized uniquely by (6,7,11). The cutoff 44 equals |tau^6(0)|.
limitations: Exactly c<=44 only; no extrapolation past the sixth substitution scale.
Universal positions proved via closure not finite sampling.
